target_customer: Brick and mortar retailers wanting in store analytics and A/B testing from their security cameras
problem: Physical stores lack the conversion data and experimentation that online stores have.
business_model: B2B SaaS analytics sold to retailers (clients included Barneys, Payomatic and Fortune 200 retailers)

founders.name: Yash Kothari
founders.background_notes: Left before the shutdown per Technical.ly.

exit.reason: Technical.ly June 2016: closed for lack of customer growth; securing a long term retail customer proved hard.

competitors.name: Prism Skylabs
competitors.what: Analyzes in store security camera footage

competitors.name: Euclid
competitors.what: Analytics for physical stores with more marketing focus

competitors.name: Nomi
competitors.what: In store analytics focused on marketing

technical_complexity.rationale: Computer vision on existing camera feeds to track customer movement, built by two students.

defensibility.rationale: Established players such as Prism Skylabs already did the same camera analysis, and retailers could switch easily.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought or copied it. The company shut down in June 2016.

market_need_then: Retailers lacked in store experimentation data, and several funded startups were chasing the same problem in 2014.

branding.name_origin: Hindi word meaning hard work or a great endeavor, and also a blend of the first three letters of each founder's first name (PRA and YAS), per a University of Pennsylvania article.
branding.domain_note: prayasanalytics.com now redirects to a domain broker, so the domain is for sale.
branding.brand_signature: Name doubling as Hindi word and founder name blend
branding.community_and_virality: Coverage in Penn News, TechCrunch, VentureBeat and Technical.ly. No community or merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: A meaningful name but limited press about the brand itself and no sign it drove growth.

outcome_analysis: Prayas started at Penn in 2014, raised $20K from Dorm Room Fund, joined YC Summer 2015 and raised about $1M in seed. It struggled to sign a long term retail customer: the cofounder later said they never effectively charged customers, chased large retailers they could not reach, and earned only $5,750 in nonrecurring revenue. It shut down in June 2016 for lack of customer growth and returned most investor money.
notes: prayasanalytics.com redirects to a domain sale page (HugeDomains), so the site is dead. The $1M seed amount is from Technical.ly; the date 2015-09 and investors 500 Startups and Birchmere Ventures come from Bouncewatch (aggregator). CB Insights shows $190K over 3 rounds, PitchBook $1.14M, Dealroom about $1M, and Latka says it raised no outside funding, which conflicts. The 2016-09 round is from CB Insights alone and postdates the June 2016 shutdown report, which may mean a late date error. Sources differ on the shutdown date (June 2016 versus October 2016).
